title: UNMAS estimates 139,000 square kilometres of Ukraine contaminated by mines and unexploded ordnance
body:
On 5 June 2025, UN News reported a briefing in New York by Paul Heslop, adviser in Ukraine for the UN Mine Action Service (UNMAS). According to UNMAS, over 20 percent of Ukraine's land, about 139,000 square kilometres, was contaminated by mines or unexploded ordnance. Two years earlier UNMAS had estimated 174,000 square kilometres, and 35,000 square kilometres had since been declared safe, allowing residents to return to their communities.

Over 800 casualties from unexploded ordnance had been documented, and over 6 million people lived in or around contaminated areas. Heslop said that for every square kilometre actually contaminated, about 100 are not but residents may still feel unable to return, which he called perceived contamination.

Manual clearance with a detector is the most thorough method but is slow and expensive, and area scanning can also declare land safe. UNMAS and about two dozen Ukrainian government entities were testing satellite and artificial intelligence tools. Heslop cited a lack of coordination among ground groups and funding and personnel shortages. Donors had committed 1 billion dollars, though the full effort would cost many billions. The report said Ukraine's agricultural sector had lost 83.9 billion dollars since the war began, partly because of contaminated farmland, and that the Food and Agriculture Organization had supported over 250,000 families with vouchers and seeds.
